decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler and Froslass for immediate Fake Out control and fast Mega Froslass pressure into the known Sneasler/Incineroar pattern. Keep Kingambit in reserve for a possible Mega Floette adjustment, with Basculegion providing strong late-game priority and Water/Ghost offense.

Drop Sinistcha (Mega-Froslass Blizzard OHKO from the notebook) and Basculegion (Choice Scarf Jolly 143 is slower than Mega Froslass Speed range 154-189 across every neutral roll, so its speed-pivot role evaporates in this match). decisions.notebook: Cross-game durable updates: Mega Froslass Blizzard in Snowscape OHKOes Sinistcha from full HP — Sinistcha does not return to any future Bring 4 unless opposing Froslass is verifiably absent from opponent's six. CRITICAL CORRECTION TO PRIOR NOTEBOOK: Sneasler CloseCombat is immune to Froslass (Ghost immunity to Fighting); Fake Out is also 0x on Froslass (Normal into Ghost). The only Sneasler move that lands on Froslass is DireClaw at NVE 0.5x (18.6-35.9%) — never plan CC into Froslass from Sneasler slot. Primary Mega-Froslass answer is Incineroar FlareBlitz (Fire SE 2x, 85.9-166.9%, often OHKO). Secondary answer is Kingambit KowtowCleave (Dark SE 2x, 98.3-233%); Kingambit's Steel typing also turns Mega-Froslass Blizzard NVE 0.5x (only 8.2-19.4% chip), making Kingambit a clean Froslass pivot — distinct from the prior Sneasler CC warning. The recorded 'Fighting->Steel/Dark 0.5x OHKO' of my Kingambit by opposing Sneasler CC was a simulator flag, not a real type weakness (Fighting into Dark/Steel is actually neutral), but the practical lesson 'never bring King raw onto healthy opposing Sneasler' still holds for low-investment King spreads. Opponent Sneasler still Fake-Outs my Incineroar for support denial; mitigate with Sitrus Berry and only commit Incineroar to confirmed-target turns. Basculegion Choice Scarf Jolly 143 is slower than Mega Froslass Speed range 154-189 across every neutral roll, so Basculegion cannot function as the Froslass speed-pivot this match — drop from Bring 4 and reserve for non-Froslass metas or late-game LastRespects cleanup. Floette-Eternal with Floettite is my only Mega option and opponent fields two Megas (Froslass, Scovillain), so Floette must be brought every game to contest the Mega slot and run Fairy coverage + late Calm Mind sweep. Future plans: (1) Bring 4 = Sneasler / Incineroar / Kingambit / Floette-Eternal; lead Sneasler + Incineroar. (2) Turn 1: Incineroar FlareBlitz onto the Froslass slot, Sneasler FakeOut or DireClaw the off-Froslass slot; pivot King onto confirmed Froslass entries. (3) Pivot Kingambit only onto locked opposing Sneasler turns (Protect, PartingShot, non-CC), never onto healthy opposing Sneasler. (4) Bench Sinistcha entirely in this matchup set; revisit only if opponent Froslass is verifiably absent from the opposing 6. (5) Bring Floette-Eternal every game for Mega parity and late Calm Mind + Dazzling Gleam wins.

If Froslass Protects (50% chance after prior use), my Sneasler takes no Blizzard risk and safely triggers Unburden.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 must-win. Foe team revealed: Sneasler (Unburden, Adamant, White Herb consumed turn 1), Froslass-Mega (Snow Warning, Timid). Backline 2 of {Kingambit/LifeOrb, Lycanroc-Dusk/FocusSash/ToughClaws, Basculegion/Adaptability, Scovillain/Mega/Moody}. CC + Unburden is a key tempo swing. Floette-Eternal remains anti-status pivot.

decisions.rationale: Both my Sneasler and Incineroar are fainted; must fill both slots with my two remaining Pokémon. Kingambit (77% HP, frozen) goes to slot 1 across from foe Sneasler, Floette-Eternal (100%) to slot 2. Even with a tough position, playing on preserves a non-zero chance to win game 2 (and the series), whereas conceding yields 0%.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 must-win (series 0-1). Foe Sneasler runs Unburden CC set with White Herb; after two CC uses sits at -2 Def/SpD—further CCs worsen its bulk but its Attack remains high. Froslass-Mega is Snow Warning pivot with Blizzard spread. Foe backline 2-of-4: Kingambit/LifeOrb, Lycanroc-Dusk/Sash/ToughClaws, Basculegion/Adaptability, Scovillain/Mega/Moody. My Kingambit carries Defiant + Sucker Punch (high-priority SE vs Froslass Ghost). Floette-Eternal's Flower Veil blocks ally status and opposing stat drops—useful insurance if Kingambit thaws and faces Intimidate or Icy Wind later. Forward plan: get Kingambit thawed, use Floette to pivot and punish Sneasler's CC self-debuffs, hunt Sucker Punch on Froslass or set up Calm Mind for Dazzling Gleam sweep.

decisions.rationale: Close Combat moves first and guarantees the KO on Kingambit, preventing any thawed attack. Blizzard then hits the lone remaining Floette at full single-target power, is fully accurate in snow, and moves before Floette.

This preserves Basculegion and minimizes the chance of losing to a surviving Floette.

decisions.rationale: Game 2 is must-win. Kingambit is frozen (80% can't move), so I pick the highest-upside line: Sucker Punch into Froslass-Mega (priority +1, SE 2x, Blackglasses boost). Froslass needs to keep Snow Warning active so it likely clicks Blizzard—opening the window for Sucker Punch to land first and threaten a KO. Even if Sucker Punch whiffs (Froslass Protects) and Sneasler CCs Kingambit for the OHKO this turn, the floor is just losing Kingambit. Floette-Eternal Mega Evolves and fires Dazzling Gleam as a spread: Sneasler is Fairy-weak (Fighting), already at -2 SpD, so it takes near-OHKO chip; Froslass takes neutral damage. Removing the Unburden-Sneasler threat this turn leaves Floette in a winnable 2v1 cleanup versus a damaged Froslass. SD/Protect on Kingambit has lower upside than pressuring Froslass, and Draining Kiss or Calm Mind on Floette concedes too much tempo in a must-win game.
decisions.notebook: Cross-game durable facts: Foe Sneasler runs Unburden + White Herb Close Combat; Froslass-Mega is the Snow Warning Blizzard pivot. Foe backline 2-of-4 not yet seen this series: Kingambit/LifeOrb, Lycanroc-Dusk/FocusSash/ToughClaws, Basculegion/Adaptability, Scovillain-Mega/Moody. My Kingambit has Defiant + Blackglasses + Sucker Punch (priority SE on Ghost); Floette-Eternal has Flower Veil (ally status/drop immunity), Calm Mind pivot, and Mega option. Kingambit is vulnerable to being frozen mid-game in Snowscape. Future plan: in game 3 (or decisive late turns), use Floette's Mega offensively only when it lands cleanly (e.g., into a non-Ice-resist core), let Kingambit's Sucker Punch threaten any Ghost/Fairy-weak switch-ins, and keep Snow Warning turns count in mind since Froslass outspeeds many pivots.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Floette-Mega with the strongest available combination. Froslass-Mega is guaranteed to move first and Blizzard is fully accurate during the final snow turn; Kowtow Cleave follows if needed. Combined damage has a strong KO chance, and even a narrow survival leaves Floette vulnerable to priority or Basculegion cleanup.
decisions.notebook: Mega Froslass at 170 Speed outspeeds every legal Timid Mega Floette range, and Blizzard is fully accurate in snow. Activated Unburden Sneasler reaches 314 Speed. Kingambit is the safest defensive response to Mega Floette's Fairy attacks. Continue respecting Choice Scarf Basculegion's Speed in future games.

decisions.rationale: I'm at 48% HP solo vs two opponents. Dazzling Gleam could KO Froslass (47% HP, damage range 34.5-62.8%) but combined counter-attacks (Blizzard 30-42.7% + Sucker Punch 26.7-38.7% = 85-122% combined) would KO me from 72 HP if Froslass survives. Calm Mind is safer: Sucker Punch fails against my status move (no attacking move used), Blizzard is reduced by +1 SpD (~22-32 damage), letting me survive at ~40-50 HP with a +1 SpA boost. Next turn my boosted Dazzling Gleam threatens OHKO on Froslass and severe damage on Kingambit. Kingambit is fainted so I pass; forfeit gives 0% series win probability while fighting on preserves my small chance.
decisions.notebook: Cross-game durable facts confirmed: Foe Kingambit is Adamant Life Orb Defiant with Sucker Punch/Kowtow Cleave; Froslass-Mega is the Snow Warning Blizzard pivot that outspeeds many threats. Foe Sneasler runs Unburden + White Herb Close Combat (off-the-board this game). Foe reserves 1-of-3 unseen: Lycanroc-Dusk/FocusSash/ToughClaws, Basculegion/Adaptability, Scovillain-Mega/Moody. My team identity: Kingambit (Defiant/Blackglasses/Sucker Punch SE on Ghost), Floette-Eternal (Flower Veil ally-protect + Calm Mind pivot, Mega = Fairy Aura offensively). Key lesson: Snow Warning turns are precious — Kingambit frozen in Snowscape cost me game 2 momentum. Future plan game 3: lead with a non-Ice-vulnerable pivot, preserve Kingambit for Sucker Punch on Ghost/Fairy-weak switches, and only commit Floette-Mega offensively into a non-Ice-resist core.

reflections.summary: The Game 2 adjustment helped rather than backfired: Sneasler, Mega Froslass, Kingambit and Basculegion matched up well, and Mega Froslass was the correct evolution. Snow-accurate Blizzard supplied decisive spread pressure, while Sneasler removed Incineroar and the opposing Kingambit. The turn-1 freeze on Kingambit was important luck because it denied multiple actions, but clean, error-free piloting converted that advantage: Froslass also KOed Sneasler and beat Mega Floette. This clinched the authoritative 2-0 series win.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same Sneasler plus Mega Froslass core and generally the same four; Basculegion was unused but remained a sound reserve. Do not plan around another freeze: proactively use Sneasler to pressure Incineroar and Kingambit, preserve Kingambit as the safest Fairy-resistant Mega Floette answer, and continue exploiting Mega Froslass's guaranteed snow Blizzard and Speed advantage.
reflections.notebook: Opponent has shown a preference for Sneasler plus Incineroar with Kingambit and Mega Floette in back, including willingness to pivot Sneasler immediately into Kingambit while Incineroar pressures Froslass. Mega Froslass at 170 Speed outruns every legal Timid Mega Floette range; Blizzard is fully accurate in snow and dealt about half to Mega Floette. Activated Unburden Sneasler reaches 314 Speed. Kingambit is the safest defensive response to Mega Floette's Fairy attacks. Continue respecting Choice Scarf Basculegion's Speed if it is brought.

reflections.summary: Lost game 2 (and the series 0-2) because my Kingambit froze on the turn-1 Blizzard from opp's Froslass-Mega in Snowscape, immediately neutralizing the one Pokémon on my team built to revenge-kill the Froslass (Sucker Punch) or punish opp's Kingambit pivot (Defiant). With Kingambit frozen I had to bench it turn 2, surrendering tempo to opp's Sneasler, which OHKO'd my Incineroar with Close Combat (4x SE on Fire/Dark) and 2HKO'd my Sneasler with the next Blizzard. My Floette-Mega only entered turn 3, Mega'd turn 4, and its Dazzling Gleam only traded for opp Sneasler — opp Froslass survived at 47% and cleaned my last Pokémon turn 5. Between-game adjustments were insufficient: the stated plan to 'lead non-Ice-vulnerable and preserve Kingambit' was abandoned when I led Sneasler+Incineroar again and pivoted Kingambit in on turn 1, the exact mistake that fed the freeze. The team-preview itself was defensible (the four brought — Sneasler, Kingambit, Incineroar, Floette — were the right tools) but the Mega timing was forced and too late: I had no opportunity to Mega on turns 1-2 and by turn 3 Snow was already established. The series is best read as 'draft correct, sequencing frozen out.'
reflections.adjustment: Lead Floette + Incineroar into opp's Froslass-Mega + Sneasler. Floette-Mega at 169 Spe outspeeds opp's Froslass and OHKOs it with Fairy-Aura Dazzling Gleam in Snowscape before Blizzard can meaningfully chip or freeze my team; Incineroar Intimidate softens opp's Blizzard and Fake Out shuts down opp Sneasler's CC. Mega Floette on turn 1 — do not delay; commit immediately so opp has to respect the Fairy Aura on the spread. Keep Kingambit on the bench: never pivot it into a live Snowscape turn (it is freeze-bait and a single freeze loses the game). Bring Kingambit in only after Snow is down or opp Froslass is dead, as a Defiant revenge-sweeper on opp Kingambit's pivot or as a Sucker-Punch response to a Froslass switch. If the 4th-mon reveal is Scovillain-Mega (Grass/Fire resists Fairy Aura), pivot to Sneasler + Incineroar instead and save Floette-Mega for after Scovillain is chipped.
reflections.notebook:
Confirmed opp profile across the series:
- Kingambit (Adamant Life Orb Defiant; Sucker Punch / Kowtow Cleave / Swords Dance / Protect). Pivots via Protect, revenge-kills Ghosts and Fairies; Kowtow Cleave threatens OHKOs on my Floette-Mega (Dark on Fairy).
- Froslass-Mega (Timid Snow Warning; Blizzard / Shadow Ball / Thunderbolt / Protect). The Snowscape lead and the entire game plan. Blizzard in Snow never misses and hits both opponents; any of my Ice-vulnerable mons that switch in risk freeze, and Steel-types like my Kingambit are especially freeze-bait. My Floette-Mega at 169 Spe outspeeds it.
- Sneasler (Adamant Unburden + White Herb; Fake Out / Close Combat / Dire Claw / Protect). Close Combat is 4x SE on my Incineroar (Fire/Dark) for a clean OHKO; the CC mirror trade also threatens my Sneasler. Has Fake Out priority to disrupt my leads.
- 4th-mon pool (one of): Lycanroc-Dusk (FocusSash ToughClaws; CC / Rock Slide / Accelerock / Protect) — bring Sneasler, CC mirror wins; Basculegion (Adaptability Mystic Water; Last Respects / Aqua Jet / Wave Crash / Protect) — Kingambit Sucker Punch on switch; Scovillain-Mega (Moody) — the dangerous one, Grass/Fire resists Fairy Aura and Moody snowballs, so lead Sucker-Punch Kingambit or Sneasler, NOT Floette.

My team identity (rebuilt from public Regulation M-B sets):
- Kingambit: Defiant / Blackglasses / Sucker Punch — priority revenge-kill on opp Froslass and opp Kingambit; Blackglasses boosts Dark STAB into Ghosts/Psychics. NEVER pivot into Snowscape.
- Floette-Eternal: Mega = Fairy Aura. Dazzling Gleam OHKOs opp Froslass in Snow and threatens opp Sneasler (Fairy on Fighting/Poison). Outspeeds opp Froslass-Mega. Mega on turn 1 in this matchup.
- Sneasler: mirror CC threat, beats Lycanroc-Dusk, threatens opp Kingambit after Defiant boost.
- Incineroar: Intimidate + Fake Out pivot. Intimidate softens opp Blizzard and opp CC; Fake Out shuts down opp Sneasler. Do NOT leave Incineroar exposed without Fake Out support — opp Sneasler CC OHKOs it.

Durable strategic lessons for a rematch:
1. Versus Froslass-Mega Snowscape leads, the correct opener is Floette-Mega + Incineroar to OHKO Froslass before Snow freezes the game.
2. Never pivot Kingambit into a live Snowscape turn — the freeze alone loses tempo and the game.
3. Mega Floette on turn 1 against this comp; delaying forfeits the offensive race against Snow chip.
4. Save Kingambit as a mid/late-game revenge-sweeper on opp Kingambit or as a Sucker-Punch response once Snow is down or Froslass is dead.
5. Opp Sneasler OHKOs Incineroar with CC — pair Incineroar with Fake Out support or pivot out on Sneasler reveal.
